#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This adds buildkit's `ControlServer` `DiskUsage()` and `Prune()` methods over buildah's local images in a new `internal/rpc/control` package. The server is not registered with the rpc server yet; this PR only adds the methods and unit tests

DiskUsage reports one `UsageRecord` per image, except manifest lists. An image is in use if a container uses it or a manifest list references it, and everything under such an image is in use too. A tagged image and everything under it are reported as shared, which Prune keeps unless `All` is set, as in buildkit. Each record's size is the image's own layer (0 for config only steps) and its parent comes from libimage's layer tree

Prune removes records that are neither in use nor shared, and shared records too when `All` is set. it removes one image at a time without removing parents automatically, never removes a tagged image and rechecks each image's names just before removing it. It stops at the first removing but stops sending. An image that a container started using is skipped.

`LastUsed`, `UsageCount` and `Description` are left unset because buildah doesnt track them. `Filter`. `AgeLimit`m `KeepDuration` and the space limits are rejected with `Unimplemented`

#### How to verify it

```
sudo go test ./internal/rpc/control -count=1 -v
sudo STORAGE_DRIVER=overlay go test ./internal/rpc/control -count=1 -v
```

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I compared this against buildkitd v0.34.1 using the same Dockerfile, and the image records line up: the base image and every step are records, intermediates arent in use and `Parents` always point at other records. The remaining differences are that there are no `source.local` or `exec.cachemount` records, config only steps get a 0 size record, sizes are file contents rather than disk usage and `All` never removes a tagged image

Questions: cache mounts are left out because `GetCacheMount`'s locking doesnt let prune tell whether a build is using one, so should i fix that in a separate PR first? Is content size acceptable or should I add a disk usage size in container libs?

comments.body: @ajoshua2004 Does this have any related issues? Why are you adding buildkit api? Is that a good idea?

@Honny1 This is part of the BuildKit LLB work. @nalind asked me to implement the Control API’s `DiskUsage` and `Prune` methods, so he’s the best person to talk about the overall direction.

Implementing `controlapi.ControlServer` means using BuildKit’s generated API types, so the methods are wire-compatible with BuildKit clients.
